title: Microsoft Tech Support Scam - Beware!!
description: Beware! If you get a call from "Microsoft" claiming your computer has been infected with a virus - IT'S A SCAM!!    Listen in to a phone call between Chris and one of these scammers.

potential_elements.text: Beware! If you get a call from "Microsoft" claiming your computer has been infected with a virus - IT'S A SCAM!! Listen in to a phone call between Chris and one of these scammers.

label_evidence.text: Beware! If you get a call from "Microsoft" claiming your computer has been infected with a virus - IT'S A SCAM!! Listen in to a phone call between Chris and one of these scammers.

textual.observation: The description reports a phone call from someone presented as "Microsoft" who claims that the listener's computer has been infected with a virus.

evidence.quote: If you get a call from "Microsoft" claiming your computer has been infected with a virus

textual.context: Presented as a warning and as a recording of a phone call; the source describes the callers as scammers, but the records do not independently establish the callers' identity or intent.
textual.potential_relevance: A claimed Microsoft affiliation is linked to an infection claim in a phone call, providing a specific identity-and-claim relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not state what action the caller requested, whether any payment or data transfer was involved, or whether the affiliation or infection claim was genuine.

visual.observation: On-screen text describes a caller presenting as Microsoft while making unsolicited requests involving personal or financial information; another frame says the caller is supposedly calling from Microsoft and asks about the viewer's iPhone and iPad.
visual.context: The material is presented as commentary about a suspected technical-support scam, including the visible quotation: "Microsoft does not send unsolicited email messages or make unsolicited phone calls to request personal or financial information, or fix your computer."
visual.potential_relevance: A claimed Microsoft affiliation is linked to requests for information about the viewer's devices and activities that could expose personal or financial information, which conditionally merits review as an identity-and-information-request cue.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish the caller's actual identity, whether the call occurred as described, or whether any information was disclosed.

visual.observation: The on-screen account says the caller attempted to provide steps for granting "REMOTE ACCESS" to the computer and describes possible access to financial and personal information and the uploading of software that would continue sending personal information.
visual.context: The source describes this as a reported interaction and later states: "I AM NOT doing any of what he is instructing me to do."
visual.potential_relevance: A requested remote-computer-access step is explicitly connected in the source to potential access to financial and personal information and continued transmission of personal information, providing a concrete mechanism cue for conditional review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show the remote-access steps being completed, software being installed, data being taken, or any resulting loss.

textual_context_notes.observation: The source explicitly warns viewers about the described calls and labels the situation as a scam.

visual_context_notes.observation: The material includes an explicit warning that Microsoft does not make unsolicited calls requesting personal or financial information or offering to fix a computer.
The narrator explicitly states that they did not follow the caller's instructions and intended to keep the caller away from real victims.
The closing frame displays the safety message "BE SAFE!!!" and the site text "RatRaceRebellion.com".

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because its stated purpose is to warn about unsolicited calls from someone presented as Microsoft, rather than promote that caller's offer or request participation. The remote-access and information-risk mechanism is discussed as commentary on a reported interaction, and the speaker says they did not follow the instructions. The closing safety message reinforces the warning, without claiming that the associated website or every discussed claim is independently safe or verified.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is a warning and investigation of a purported technical-support interaction: it questions the caller's Microsoft claim, describes the requested remote-access mechanism, states that the instructions were not followed, and ends with a safety warning.

evidence.observation: The description warns about calls from someone presented as Microsoft who claims that the recipient's computer has a virus.
evidence.quote: Beware! If you get a call from "Microsoft" claiming your computer has been infected with a virus - IT'S A SCAM!!

evidence.observation: The displayed text states that Microsoft does not make unsolicited phone calls to request personal or financial information or to fix a computer.
The displayed commentary says the caller is supposedly calling from Microsoft and questions why the caller is asking about an iPhone and iPad.
The displayed account says the caller expects computer access and asks what the computer is used for, including whether it is used for banking, paying bills or purchases.

The displayed text describes instructions to give the caller remote access and attributes to the caller the possibility of obtaining financial and personal information or uploading software that continues sending personal information.
The displayed speaker states that they are not doing what the caller instructed and that the caller tried three different ways to obtain computer access.
The closing frame displays the warning "BE SAFE!!!".
